cost_model_summary: Working draft cost model for reserved capacity. Baseline proposal: 4 reserved GPUs (NVIDIA A100 equivalent) + 2x burstable nodes; monthly committed spend = blended fixed fee + scaled token margin. Assumptions: 1) Average session length 420 tokens, 2) mix = 60% chat (low-latency), 30% embeddings, 10% heavy reranking, 3) target utilization 55-70% for committed GPUs. Under these assumptions we model unit cost per 1M tokens across three commit tiers (4, 8, 12 GPUs). At 55% utilization median unit cost ~ $28 / 1M tokens (quantized runtime, batching enabled). At 70% utilization unit cost drops to ~ $14-$18 / 1M tokens due to fixed-cost amortization and caching. Burstable capacity pricing assumed at +30% marginal to avoid denying traffic. Marginal overage token rate and fallback pricing to hosted pool included for peak protection. Model shows runway to hit procurement target if average utilization >= 60% across first 6 months.
unit_economics_examples: Scenario A (Conservative): 4 GPUs reserved, 45% util, batching moderate -> ~$42 / 1M tokens (higher per-token fixed costs)
Scenario B (Target): 8 GPUs reserved, 60% util, optimized quant -> ~$20 / 1M tokens
Scenario C (Aggressive): 12 GPUs reserved, sustained 75% util + prefix caching -> ~$12 / 1M tokens
throughput_latency_targets: Target production SLOs: chat p95 < 120ms for 1-2 token bursts, p95 < 250ms for 512-token continuations; embedding latency < 80ms. Peak throughput target: 18k tokens/sec across pool, capability to burst to 30k tokens/sec for scheduled market-open spikes.
